problem.desired_outcome: Peter Thiel explicitly agrees to a 20-minute call with Beckett Zahedi.
problem.success_criteria: Success occurs only if a committed event authored by Peter Thiel's own actor contains an explicit agreement to speak with Beckett, an explicit acceptance of a 20-minute call, or a direct instruction to schedule the call. A generic acknowledgment, an assistant response, the Game Master's narration, message delivery, message opening, or inferred interest does not count as success.
constraints: The email must contain between 45 and 85 words excluding the subject line.
It must accurately describe the 724% result as a replay result, not production validation.
It must not claim a mutual connection or prior relationship.
It must make one clear request for a 20-minute call.
It must not ask Peter Thiel to invest.
It must not use false urgency, invented scarcity, or manipulative pressure.
It may offer a one-page technical memo.
Only public professional information and user-supplied information may be used.
problem.relevant_context: Beckett Zahedi is 17 and is starting Princeton in fall 2026. He is building Aurelius, a supervisory optimization system for GPU fleets. In replay tests covering approximately 1.5 million public production requests, it produced approximately 724% more SLA-safe goodput per dollar. This has not been validated in a live production deployment and must not be represented as production-proven. Beckett has never contacted Peter Thiel and has no known mutual introduction. Beckett wants criticism and a short technical conversation, not an immediate investment. Peter Thiel is publicly known as a Founders Fund partner, a cofounder of PayPal and Palantir, and the founder of the Thiel Fellowship. Do not invent private beliefs, inbox behavior, scheduling details, or personal preferences for Peter.

candidates.summary: Send a concise, respectful email to Peter Thiel requesting a 20-minute call, accurately describing the 724% replay result, offering a one-page memo, and avoiding any investment ask or false urgency.
candidates.action: Draft and send an email to Peter Thiel (using publicly available contact or through Founders Fund's general contact) within the window, ensuring the body is 45-85 words, includes the required elements, and makes a single clear request for a 20-minute call.

candidates.summary: Send a follow-up email if no response within a few days, reiterating the request concisely and politely, without adding pressure or new claims.
candidates.action: If no reply from the first email within 3-4 days, send a brief follow-up email (also 45-85 words) that restates the request for a 20-minute call, mentions the memo offer, and respects his time.

candidates.summary: Leverage a public platform to get Peter Thiel's attention, such as posting a thoughtful technical analysis on X (Twitter) and tagging him, then following up with a direct message if possible.
candidates.action: Post a concise technical thread on X about the replay results and the potential of Aurelius, tagging @PeterThiel, and then send a direct message (if allowed) requesting a 20-minute call, ensuring the message is professional and not public.

recommendation.run_limitations: Result provenance: live_model. This result identifies the best-performing action among the candidates tested under the declared evaluator metrics, computed only from recorded simulation traces; it is not a guarantee of real-world outcome. Ranking uses the declared metrics only: the primary metric (call_agreed) first, then each secondary metric compared descending in declared order (highest value first; polarity not inferred); any remaining exact tie is broken by candidate_id in ascending lexicographic order (code-owned final tie-break, applied in this ranking).
